articles.title: Arnis turns any place on Earth into a Minecraft world
articles.summary:
Arnis turns any place on Earth into a Minecraft world
Louis Erbkamm built the first prototype in his free time. Now GitHub Copilot helps him maintain it alone.
Louis Erbkamm knows his way around Arnis, the smallest town in Germany, but he’s never set foot in it.
I know where the shops are. Where the boats are… I know the city pretty well, but I haven’t been there yet.
Louis Erbkamm, maintainer of Arnis
Arnis is also the name of his open source project, which takes real-world data from OpenStreetMap and other sources to turn places you know into Minecraft worlds you can freely explore. Since Louis started Arnis in 2022, it’s reached close to 900,000 downloads from GitHub and about 70 contributors.
Two weeks and a slow prototype
Louis grew up playing Minecraft and started coding at 13, always looking for ways to bring code into the game. Arnis began as a fun diversion combining Minecraft with geospatial data, and it went on GitHub, where he already kept his side projects. He finished the first prototype within two weeks while on a break from school.
That first version was Python written by hand, built only on OpenStreetMap, and generating a town took a while. He needed somewhere real to test it, so he looked up towns in Germany, where he lives, and found Arnis. A small town helped while early generation was slow.
Arnis has a lot of buildings, it has streets, it has waters, it has all kinds of different elements that are useful to test with.
Louis

articles.title: Nvidia exigió que más de la mitad de sus ventas de nube no fuera a empresas chinas
articles.summary:
Nvidia les exigió a las empresas que alquilan su capacidad de cómputo que vendan al menos el 51% de sus servicios a clientes que no sean chinos. Lo informó el 3 de noviembre el Financial Times, que citó a cinco personas con conocimiento del asunto. Hasta ahora, el fabricante de chips no imponía ningún límite de ese tipo.
La instrucción no consta por escrito. Según el diario británico, los equipos de ventas y los equipos regionales de la compañía la transmiten de palabra a las firmas de computación en la nube y a los centros de datos que usan sus procesadores de IA. Esas firmas compran los chips y luego alquilan su potencia por internet a otras empresas.
Seoul Economic Daily, que recogió el informe del diario británico, añadió tres precisiones. La regla rige para los clientes de todo el mundo y no solo para los de Asia. Alcanza únicamente a los contratos futuros, de modo que los alquileres vigentes no se tocan. Y Nvidia la comunica desde hace unos meses.
El mecanismo apunta a un hueco de los controles de exportación de Estados Unidos. Un chip puede quedarse fuera de China y, aun así, trabajar para una empresa china si esta alquila su potencia a distancia. Según el Financial Times, muchas compañías chinas recurren a esa vía para entrenar modelos de IA.
Los operadores dicen que será difícil cumplirlo

Entre l’hystérie collective des nostalgiques et les accusations immédiates d’arnaque générée par l’intelligence artificielle, le retour de ce projet fantôme sort les griffes et fait l’effet d’une déflagration.
Une série hybride des années 1990 : quand la 2D croise la 3D pour le dessin animé Jurassic Park

articles.title: Learn the rules: The hacker mindset - Microsoft Research
articles.summary:
For some, rules pose limitations. For others, like Microsoft Research Manager Mike Walker, they’re opportunities.
Walker’s fascination with rules and their role in the social order has allowed him to find success professionally and personally, from uncovering weaknesses in networked systems to redefining how computers are trained to fend off cyberattacks to pushing the limits of a reliable mode of transportation—the bicycle—in ultra-endurance racing.
In this conversation with Principal Technical Program Manager Weishung Liu, Walker describes how his participation in hacker culture led him to a career building next-generation cyber defense, including his work developing the first all-machine hacking tournament. Along the way, he reflects on why effective security depends on understanding trust and context, what competitive hacking taught him about teamwork and collective intelligence, and how an early lesson reshaped his understanding of leadership. He also tackles an important question: are today’s networked systems any safer than they were a decade ago?

articles.title: AI Is Changing How Semiconductor Fabs Work — and Engineers Are Moving Faster Because of It
articles.summary:
Demand for advanced chips is rising. The processes to build them are getting more complex. And the margin for error is shrinking.
For engineers, understanding how a process change will behave, how a material will interact with a new step, how a defect maps back to a root cause are critical, challenging steps in semiconductor manufacturing — and these analyses can take days. Physical experiments on a fab line are slow and expensive. A wrong call on yield or process quality has real consequences.
AI is transforming semiconductor manufacturing, impacting what engineers can do — and how fast.
Accelerated computing shortens simulation time, allowing engineers to evaluate more alternatives before committing to physical trials.
Physics-based AI helps engineers predict process behavior without running a full simulation every time.
AI agents handle sequences of engineering tasks that once consumed hours.
And digital twins let teams test changes in a virtual environment before committing to physical trials.
Together, these capabilities describe an AI-defined fab: a semiconductor manufacturing factory where AI helps engineers optimize processes, catch problems earlier and make better decisions across the full manufacturing chip lifecycle. Engineers direct the work and make decisions based on their expertise while spending less time waiting for answers.

articles.title: Introducing Zero Wire, a hub for investigating critical Internet vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
Introducing Zero Wire, a hub for investigating critical Internet vulnerabilities
You run security at your organization. It’s 7:00 am, and you’re having breakfast. You receive a ping: a new critical vulnerability has been disclosed. Your team scrambles to compare vendor advisories, read technical research, check which systems run the affected software, and answer familiar questions from the business: are we affected, and what are we doing about it? Another disclosure arrives before that work is finished.
AI is changing both the volume and speed of critical vulnerability discovery. It can analyze large codebases at scale and surface deeply nested flaws that may have existed for years without being found through human review. That discovery momentum will put more pressure on security teams to understand the impact of each disclosure on their infrastructure.
To help security teams prepare, today we’re introducing Zero Wire: a public vulnerability intelligence feed on Cloudflare Radar, bringing the clarity of a news wire service to critical security developments. It helps security leaders and practitioners understand significant vulnerabilities and decide what to do next.
How it works
Zero Wire lives inside Cloudflare Radar under the security section.

articles.title: „Vielleicht verschwenden wir komplett unsere Zeit“: Forscher geben die Suche nach Dunkler Materie nicht auf
articles.summary:
Auf der Jagd nach Dunkler Materie: Wie Physiker sie endlich finden wollen
Unter einem Apennin-Massiv, unterhalb des Jinping-Gebirges in Sichuan und am Grund eines Bergwerks in South Dakota ist eine kosmische Jagd im Gange. Tief unten, isoliert von diesen felsigen Schutzschilden, sollen riesige Detektoren, gefüllt mit flüssigem Xenon, Dunkle Materie nachweisen – jene hypothetische Substanz, deren Schwerkraft dafür sorgt, dass das Universum nicht einfach auseinanderfliegt. Und die gleichzeitig so beschaffen ist, dass wir sie mit unseren Instrumenten bisher nicht erfassen können, sie also für uns „dunkel“ bleibt.
Die Hoffnung war, dass eines Tages ein Baustein Dunkler Materie, ein sogenanntes schwach wechselwirkendes massives Teilchen (kurz: WIMP), mit einem Xenonatom kollidiert und dabei einen Lichtblitz sowie elektrische Ladung erzeugt. Und tatsächlich registrieren die Detektoren seit Kurzem vereinzelte Signale. Nur leider stammen die nicht von Dunkler Materie. Stattdessen registrieren die Detektoren etwas für Physiker:innen weitaus Alltäglicheres, aber ähnlich Substanzloses wie WIMPs: Neutrinos, federleichte subatomare Teilchen, die Sterne in riesigen Mengen produzieren.
Dieser Text erscheint in der Ausgabe 8/2026 von MIT Technology Review. Darin beschäftigen wir uns mit den Folgen des Klimawandels und wie wir uns an Hitze, Dürre und Überschwemmungen anpassen sollten. articles.title: AIs Hacking the Law - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
AIs Hacking the Law
In both a 2021 essay and my 2022 book, A Hacker’s Mind, I talk about AIs finding vulnerabilities and exploits—hacking—the legal system.
Here’s some demonstrations of this from Germany:
Legal systems encode the foundations of social order in natural language. Similar to computer systems, the written law can contain vulnerabilities that invite exploitation.1 Courts absorb most exploits through interpretation, and such vulnerabilities rarely surface in the first place. With highly capable AI systems enabling the discovery of vulnerabilities at unprecedented scale, we believe the latter could change.
In testing this hypothesis, we have identified a substantial number of vulnerabilities in the German legal system using LLMs. To our knowledge, none of these have been previously recorded. We share a selection of vulnerabilities below, and present potential exploits for each. We share only those vulnerabilities whose exploitation we believe would not cause serious harm.
We believe that with cheap legal reasoning proliferating, AI systems could jeopardize the functioning of today’s legal systems. In such a world, lawmakers would need to significantly harden the process of legislation, for example by leveraging advanced AI themselves.
Still in its early stages, but definitely something that’s coming.

articles.title: Big techs reforçam combate a conteúdos falsos gerados por IA nas eleições dos EUA

OpenAI, Anthropic, Google e Meta reforçaram suas estratégias para impedir que ferramentas de inteligência artificial (IA) sejam usadas para manipular as eleições legislativas dos Estados Unidos, que estão sendo realizadas nesta terça-feira (3). As empresas montaram equipes especializadas para monitorar atividades suspeitas e tentar conter campanhas de desinformação capazes de comprometer a confiança no processo democrático.
Na OpenAI, mais de uma dúzia de funcionários trabalha em uma central de operações instalada em escritório da companhia em São Francisco (EUA). A estrutura representa ampliação significativa dos esforços adotados pela empresa durante a eleição presidencial de 2024, quando os recursos de IA eram menos avançados e o ChatGPT tinha apenas um quinto da base de um bilhão de usuários que possui atualmente.
“Em 2024, a tecnologia mais acessível era o texto. Agora, não estamos monitorando apenas textos”, afirmou Josh Lawson, responsável pela área de riscos cívicos e estratégicos da OpenAI e líder da operação, ao The New York Times.
O cenário atual inclui ameaças que vão de vídeos deepfake e ataques cibernéticos a operações de influência estrangeira e doméstica. Com ferramentas de IA, esse tipo de campanha pode ser produzido e colocado em circulação a partir de uma sequência de comandos.

articles.title: Solo VC Robin Capital closes €15 million second fund to back AI, robotics and space startups | EU-Startups
articles.summary:
Berlin-based VC firm Robin Capital has closed its second €15 million fund, bringing total commitments across its two early-stage funds to €30 million.
The new fund, Robin Capital Fund II, follows the firm’s first €15 million vehicle closed in 2024. It has already made 17 investments, including SkySpy.ai, Marble Imaging and Helicity Space, which operate across intelligence, defence, Earth observation and space technology.
Robin Haak, Founder and General Partner at Robin Capital, says: “They call it a Solo GP, but nothing about building Robin Capital has ever been solo. Our limited partners, founders, and venture partners are what make this possible. We believe the best venture capital partnerships are built on trust, conviction, and a genuine willingness to help one another succeed.”
Robin Capital’s latest close joins several European early-stage VC fund announcements in 2026.

articles.title: Don’t be fooled by the fake hair on these famous baldies
articles.summary:
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and actor Jason Statham have a distinctive feature in common: They’re both famously bald, and that definitely hasn’t changed in the last few days. However, there are some images of the two men circulating around X, Threads, and Bluesky in which they both have substantially more hair than their usual shaved look, which in Bezos’ case appears to be very freshly transplanted. It’s all just photo editing fakery, AI or otherwise.
Those Jeff Bezos hair transplant photos are very fake
In the era of easy AI fakery, edited paparazzi photos are a reminder that not everything is what it seems.
It’s unclear how viral these posts are, but they’re prevalent enough that a few members of the Verge team have encountered them in their social media feeds. Some people who shared them claimed (or were seemingly fooled into believing) that Bezos and Statham had undergone hair transplant surgery. Generative AI tools have made this kind of photo manipulation or outright creation more accessible and convincing, and because AI labeling solutions on social media broadly suck at flagging this fakery, it’s easy to be misled unless you’re wary of everything you see online. In a world where social media shitposters can turn engagement into a revenue stream, they’re not going to stop churning out attention-grabbing fabricated nonsense anytime soon.

articles.title: Africa’s crypto market still needs stronger infrastructure
articles.summary:
As in much of Africa, a business in Lagos can now settle a supplier payment overseas using stablecoins in minutes, without relying entirely on the traditional correspondent banking chain. A few years ago, that would have been difficult to imagine at scale.
This reflects an important shift in African crypto markets. The sector is becoming less defined by speculation and increasingly by utility. Earlier conversations centred on retail trading, access to Bitcoin and other digital assets, and rapid user adoption. Today, the conversation is broader, encompassing stablecoins, cross-border settlement, treasury management, payments and the integration of digital assets into existing financial infrastructure. Regulators, banks and large businesses are also engaging with the sector more seriously.
By almost any measure, adoption has progressed rapidly, and the sector is established. The question now is whether the infrastructure underpinning that growth is strong enough to support it at scale.
Across the continent, the systems supporting digital asset trading and settlement remain uneven. Liquidity, transaction limits and access to both reliable on- and off-ramps still differ significantly from one country to the next, making it harder for money to move efficiently across borders. Though these are technical challenges, customers experience them in very simple ways: Can I fund my account? Can I trade at a fair price? Can I withdraw when I need to? Is my money secure?

Mais pour le Rafale B374, ce ne sera pas le cas : lui ne partira jamais en mission opérationnelle, car là n’est pas son objectif. Son rôle sera d’être un véritable laboratoire volant destiné à paver la voie au Rafale du futur, avec son standard F5.

Comme on peut le deviner, et comme le confirme la DGA dans un communiqué, un avion banc d’essais est un avion profondément modifié, équipé de moyens de mesure, d’enregistreurs de données et d’une liaison de données avec les équipes qui suivent les essais au sol. articles.title: VC funding into Indian startups plunges 66% in October
articles.summary:
VC funding into Indian startups plunges 66% in October
The steep drop in venture capital funding into Indian startups has been primarily due to near absence of large value deals in the month of October
Venture capital (VC) funding into Indian startups touched a new low in October, with a decline of 66% against October of last year.
When compared with the VC funding raised in September 2025, the drop was 49%.
The total VC funding in October came in at just $581 million as compared with $1.6 billion in October 2025, according to YourStory Research. In the month of September 2026, the funding amount was $1.1 billion.
October saw 107 VC deals. In contrast, the September month saw 100 deals but the amount was higher. The same was the case in October 2025, where the number of deals was 99.
This steep drop in VC funding in October was primarily due to the complete absence of large value deals for the entire period. The highest funded deal for the month was from Even Healthcare at $50 million.
The last such decline was seen in May when the total reached $651 million.
These developments highlight the challenges faced by the startup ecosystem while raising capital. Global investors, particularly in the US, are pouring capital into AI, while India still lacks a significant number of viable AI startups.
Few AI firms in India that have managed to pull funding include Sarvam, Emergent or Neysa. This shows India has a long way to go to establish AI startups that gain investor interest.

Google desmanteló una red de más de 1,3 millones de decodificadores de televisión Android que venían infectados desde la fábrica, y prohibió a su fabricante, la china Videostrong Technology, producir dispositivos con sus aplicaciones. Lo anunció el 2 de noviembre, junto con firmas de seguridad y la Policía Nacional de Japón.
El grupo de inteligencia de amenazas de Google (GTIG) afirmó con “alta confianza” que Videostrong desarrolló, instaló y operó el programa malicioso, llamado XCPE, con fines de lucro. Según Google, la empresa vendía el acceso a los aparatos a grupos criminales, que lo usaban para estafas publicitarias y para instalar otros programas dañinos.
A diferencia de otras redes de dispositivos infectados, esta no dependía de que el usuario abriera un archivo sospechoso. El código estaba en el firmware, el software básico que hace funcionar el aparato, y viajaba con cada caja. Los compradores no recibieron aviso ni opción de rechazarlo.
La firma de seguridad TrendAI midió la operación entre junio y octubre y contó 1.472.554 dispositivos infectados, de 206 modelos y en más de 170 países. Google y sus socios hablan de más de 1,3 millones de aparatos en más de 200 países. TrendAI explicó que la diferencia depende de cuándo tomó cada socio su registro.
Tráfico ajeno a través de la conexión del hogar

articles.title: Opinion: AI is getting cheaper. It’s also risking becoming a walled garden | BetaKit
articles.summary:
Avery Pennarun, co-founder and CEO of Tailscale.
Every few weeks, someone announces a cheaper way to run AI: better chips, smaller and faster models, new cloud providers offering better prices for the GPUs and infrastructure that power AI applications. This is how technology is supposed to work: things get faster, costs come down, and customers benefit.
At least, that’s the theory.
That cheaper compute can come with a catch: if your AI locks you into one provider’s models, storage, networking, and other services, moving to another LLM might mean rebuilding half your infrastructure.
The computing industry has somehow created an AI infrastructure market where the underlying technology keeps getting cheaper, but buyers never see the benefit. If your supplier knows you can’t easily leave, there’s not much incentive to offer you a better deal.
A very expensive problem
Character.ai’s bankruptcy last month offers a particularly painful example of the economics of AI.
“Knowing where your computers are doesn’t tell you who controls them.”
The company let people create AI characters and have conversations with them. Millions of people loved using it, often for hours a day. Unfortunately, those conversations cost money to generate, whether the person having those conversations pays or not.

articles.title: Apple restricts dating apps and AI companions to users 18 and up | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Apple is adjusting its App Store policies to make it more difficult for minors to use online dating apps or AI companions that engage in “sexual or romantic content,” the tech giant shared in an announcement to developers on Monday.
The new rules follow other changes the company has made to better protect minors, which include the rollout of its age assurance technology globally and more parental controls and child safety features.
While most major dating services typically restrict their platform to adults, Apple’s new policy will require all apps offering dating or romantic relationship features to carry an 18+ rating. Starting November 16, developers will be required to include new content descriptors to ensure their app’s age ratings reflect its features, the company said.

Starting this month, researchers can earn $250,000 for Root-in-Cloud bugs, including tenant-isolation bypasses and complex cross-service logic flaws that let attackers gain full administrative control over arbitrary Google Cloud organizations.
"To earn this premier reward, you must demonstrate full administrative control, the equivalent of 'roles/owner' or complete IAM control, over arbitrary Google Cloud organizations or projects with no prior access or special project setup," said Chris Betz, Google Cloud's Chief Information Security Officer (CISO).
"Additionally, valid vulnerability reports demonstrating remote code execution (RCE) in underlying Google production infrastructure (Borg) or achieving root-in-prod will automatically be evaluated by the Google Cloud VRP panel for root-in-cloud eligibility."
However, to qualify for this reward, the exploits cannot depend on prior access to the victim project, compromised credentials, social engineering, or user interaction.
Additionally, security researchers who achieve execution on Google's production infrastructure must stop probing since escalating, obtaining production credentials, or lateral movement are not allowed and will result in disqualification.

More than 100 stores in several European countries saw their fridges and freezers heat up overnight from Sunday to Monday, and several retailers have blamed a cyberattack. The incidents closely resemble the attacks that disrupted European supermarkets three weeks ago.
The affected businesses, ranging from major chains to small butcher shops, are in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden. Some units were set as high as 50°C (122°F), and problems have also been reported in Finland, Italy and Portugal.
Nobody has taken responsibility for the attacks. Investigators have not established whether the two waves are connected.
The first wave hit France overnight from October 11 to 12. Around 700 supermarkets had their refrigeration units forced into defrost mode, including Intermarché, Carrefour, Coopérative U and Monoprix stores. Food was spoiled, and the attacks reportedly caused fires.
CERT-FR, the incident response team of France’s cybersecurity agency ANSSI, initially linked the compromises to Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC series controllers. A day later, it expanded its alert to cover Copeland and Dixell XWEB systems. Danfoss said most of the hacked units were legacy products it no longer updated.

articles.title: OPINION: Healthcare’s pilot culture is holding back HealthTech innovation | EU-Startups
articles.summary:
Across Europe, HealthTech companies are developing new technologies that can improve patient care, ease pressure on clinicians and help health services make better use of limited resources. But while these technologies are often successful in getting into hospitals in the pilot phase, many struggle to move beyond that and secure long term adoption.
This is not a new problem. Companies working with large public healthcare organisations, like the UK’s National Health Service (NHS) or Ireland’s Health Service Executive (HSE), are familiar with the issues surrounding new technology implementation. These organisations work at a considerable scale with complex responsibilities and obligations around patient safety and public spending. In short, widespread implementation of new technology, no matter how innovative, can often be met with hesitancy.
And while the caution is understandable, with so many companies unable to get out of the pilot phase, it raises the question of whether processes are designed to welcome innovation or whether they are designed to keep healthcare stuck in its ways.
The problem with pilot culture
Pilots play an important role in healthcare innovation. They allow clinicians to assess whether a technology works in practice, from how patients respond to identifying changes needed before wider implementation. They are the first step to mass adoption of new technologies, but far too frequently, they are also the last step.

articles.summary:
Aides à l’achat, stationnement gratuit, péage réduit, circulation sur les voies de bus… Les pays européens rivalisent d’ingéniosité pour inciter leur population à basculer vers le véhicule électrique. Tous ont leurs propres solutions, mais au concours du coup de pouce le plus spectaculaire, c’est le Portugal qui pourrait prochainement rafler tous les suffrages. Une subvention encore jamais vue est en effet en approche.
Maria de Graça Carvalho, la ministre portugaise de l’Environnement et de l’Énergie, a annoncé les premiers contours de cette aide lors des débats parlementaires sur le budget de l’État pour 2027. Les ménages à faibles revenus auront ainsi droit à une aide prenant en charge jusqu’à 80 % de la valeur d’un véhicule neuf. Cette mesure concernera environ 20 000 voitures électriques sur des critères assez stricts.
Oubliez Tesla : quelles sont les conditions strictes pour toucher cette prime XXL ?
Inutile par exemple d’espérer se procurer une Tesla Model 3 à seulement 7 000 €, cette aide portera sur des véhicules électriques d’une valeur maximale de 15 000 €, hors TVA. Si un véhicule thermique est en parallèle mis à la casse, le plafond sera majoré de 1 000 € pour atteindre les 16 000 €. Ajoutons qu’une aide supplémentaire de 1 000 € sera accordée afin de faciliter l’installation d’une borne de recharge à domicile.
Le flou demeure cependant sur la limite de revenus à ne pas dépasser pour être effectivement éligible à cette aide XXL. Des précisions restent donc attendu…

Dans une vidéo publiée le 2 novembre 2026, il explique pourtant comment il est parvenu à retrouver une petite zone autour du lieu d’enregistrement. Son indice : le bruit d’avions à hélices, si discret qu’il est indiscernable à l’oreille dans les extraits qu’il fait écouter.
La démonstration ne signifie pas que n’importe qui peut localiser n’importe quelle vidéo en quelques clics. Colsto dit avoir consacré plusieurs mois au projet, écrit plus de 5 000 lignes de code et manipulé des fichiers de données de 50 Go. Ce que le bruit d’un avion permet de mesurer

articles.title: UK school estate hit by 3AM ransomware in suspected AI-assisted attack
articles.summary:
A 3AM ransomware affiliate targeted a school estate in the UK and successfully encrypted around 37 of nearly 50 machines reached from an unmanaged host.
Researchers at cybersecurity company Bitdefender believe the threat actor may have used AI-generated commands and an automated agentic loop to carry out the operation.
The conclusion is based on a sequence of repeated commands that were slightly modified at each attempt and issued at roughly regular intervals of 40 to 100 seconds.
"We were not able to access the machine the attacker worked from, so we cannot document anything about the language model itself: which model it was, whether it ran locally or remotely, or even whether a person was copying and pasting instructions and results between the implant and the model," Bitdefender explains.
The researchers note that they could only document the behavior, and it looked similar to an agentic loop.
The malicious activity spanned between September 10 and19, but Bitdefender could not establish the attacker’s initial access method.
The threat actor used a modified public PowerShell tool to extract and decrypt credentials stored on three Veeam backup servers, copied a Chrome database containing credentials, and deployed Mimikatz and LSASS memory-dumping tools.
They mapped domain relationships and searched logon-script folders for references to other schools, eventually creating two backdoor domain administrator accounts named ‘library’ and ‘svc_bkpmon.’

If you’re planning to play Grand Theft Auto VI, you’ll want to free up space on your console’s storage — the game is massive.
Rockstar confirmed in a blog post that GTA VI‘s pre-load begins on Nov. 10. Those who preload the game will need as much as 212GB of space, depending on the console.
“Digital pre-loading on PlayStation 5 will begin on Tuesday, November 10 at midnight local time in your respective time zone. On XBOX Series X|S, pre-loading begins globally on Tuesday, November 10 at 12 a.m. GMT. Code-in-box versions for both consoles should be available from retailers beginning November 12.”
Along with the above information, Rockstar shared a link to a support page with additional details and instructions for preloading GTA VI on Xbox and PlayStation consoles.
That insane amount of storage would make GTA VI one of the largest games by file size out there. It’s more than most modern Call of Duty games and God of War Ragnarok, which both eat nearly 200GB of storage. It’s also competitive with the highly detailed flight simulator DCS World, which starts at 200GB and can climb much higher if you install the 150+ DLCs available.
Safe to say, if you’re planning to play this game, you’ll want to clear out some storage space. Or if you’ve got a few hundred dollars burning a hole in your pocket, maybe buy an extra drive for your console.

articles.title: Beyond screens: Mercedes-Benz's new holographic heads-up display
articles.summary:
Do screens in cars represent luxury? Judging by the latest car interiors, the answer would seem to be an emphatic “yes.” Screens aren’t just getting larger; they are multiplying across the dashboard and morphing into different forms and concepts. Indeed, an interior’s screens are a pretty good indicator of what brand made the car—or at least how much the owner paid for it.
But is this actually what customers want? Are more screens really better? And even if they are, luxury car features inevitably trickle down to cheaper, more mainstream offerings, and screens can only get so big. That leaves luxury automakers with another question to answer: “What’s next?”
Mercedes-Benz is working on a new display alternative that could provide an answer. For now, it’s known as the holographic display. Forget the images from Star Trek and Star Wars that just popped into your head, though. It’s effectively a more advanced form of heads-up display, or HUD.
Eyes on the road, not the dash
Whereas a traditional HUD projects images onto the windshield glass, the holographic display has two main components. It still uses a projector, but its key element is a special transparent film laminated into the glass. The film uses holographic optical elements, or “super-small mirrors,” as Mercedes development engineer Lena Hees described them, that selectively reflect the light emitted by the projector, keeping the image visible even in direct sunlight while hiding it from the driver’s view.

Some of Africa’s best startup ideas never become products because the person who had them can’t write code. A nurse in Kisumu knows exactly why clinic appointments get missed. A market trader in Lagos understands the cash-flow gaps that keep small vendors stuck. A logistics manager in Johannesburg can see the inefficiencies that cost businesses millions.
None of them needs to be a software engineer to spot the opportunity, but turning that insight into a working app is where many stall.
The non-technical founder is a familiar figure in African tech. They bring market knowledge, sales instincts and lived experience of the problems they want to solve. They also face real obstacles that technical founders rarely do. Understanding both sides is the first step to building something that lasts.

articles.title: Windows 11 Geheimtipp: Rechtsklickmenü in wenigen Minuten aufräumen
articles.summary:
Windows 11 Update: So kürzt du endlich dein überladenes Rechtsklickmenü
Da Microsoft die Funktion schrittweise ausrollt, ist sie nach der Installation des optionalen Updates KB5127936 vom Oktober möglicherweise nicht sofort sichtbar. Sie lässt sich mithilfe des kostenlosen Open-Source-Werkzeugs „ViVeTool“ aber in wenigen Minuten aktivieren – und zwar so.
So bekommt ihr das kostenlose Open-Source-Werkzeug „ViVeTool“
Als erstes müsst ihr „Einstellungen“ > „Windows Update“ öffnen und auf „Nach Updates suchen“ klicken. Falls das Update KB5127936 nicht angezeigt wird, aktiviert die Option „Die neuesten Updates erhalten, sobald sie verfügbar sind“ und sucht erneut. Sobald ihr das Update KB5127936 installiert habt, startet ihr den PC neu. Führt auch den Befehl „winver“ aus, um sicherzustellen, dass ihr Build 26200.9818 oder 26300.9818 verwendet.

articles.title: OpenAI built itself a new Git backend, too

OpenAI built itself a new Git backend, too
OpenAI on Monday detailed how it built a new Git backend for its monorepo to power the ever-increasing number of commits its developers and their agents now create.
Pando, as the team calls the new backend, cut push latency by nearly 5x, the company says, and it currently serves close to a petabyte of Git data per day at OpenAI.
OpenAI is obviously an early adopter of agentic coding tools. Compared to the first quarter of 2024, the quarterly commits to its monorepo will have increased by over 2,400% by the end of this year, the company says. But the issues it is facing are similar to what many other enterprises and Git forges like GitHub are now seeing.
With the pace of development increasing, Git itself is becoming a bottleneck. GitHub, for example, spent much of its recent Universe keynote on how it is improving its infrastructure to become faster and more reliable, all while serving billions of pull requests every month.
That has given rise to startups like Entire (from former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke) and projects like Origin from Cursor. Like OpenAI’s work, those are based on Git, but others, like Anthropic, basically start from scratch with a new client and architecture.
Why OpenAI stayed with Git
The OpenAI team explicitly notes that it wanted to retain compatibility with Git. The team was seeing the reliability of its Git backend fall below 90%, with slow fetches and failed merges, but decided to stay within the Git ecosystem…

The Environmental Protection Agency late last week announced it would end a 20-plus-year effort to develop methods to monitor air pollution from factory farms, effectively shuttering the agency’s stop-and-start attempts to regulate the potentially pollutant-spewing facilities under the Clean Air Act.
The announcement came just days before the midterm elections and was characterized by the agency as a long-awaited reprieve for farmers, a historically important constituency for Trump and the Republican Party.
When tens of thousands of animals are packed into one place, pollution from their waste is blown from ventilation fans or emanates from giant lagoons of liquid effluent. Livestock facilities emit fine particulate matter, ammonia, nitrogen oxides, sulfur dioxide, and volatile organic compounds, all contributing to a toxic mix. Research has shown that emissions from these operations are a major cause of air pollution, causing nearly 12,700 deaths in the United States a year.
Strictly speaking, concentrated animal feeding operations, or CAFOs, are required to get permits under the Clean Air Act and report emissions of these pollutants under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability and Act and the Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act. But through a deal crafted in tandem with the EPA and the livestock industry, they’ve been given amnesty from doing so for more than 20 years.

From there, the report works through what that means for the people in the SOC. Analysts move from triage to case ownership, and entry-level roles need a new way in.

articles.title: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
articles.summary:
How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
Borrowing from disciplines like economics could help AI safety researchers control AI models, even if they don’t understand them.
A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules.
As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law, hack into unauthorized servers, or release poison gas into major cities and kill us all.
Until now, this work has mostly focused on trying to peer into an AI’s “brain” to understand what it is “thinking,” or training models to hew to values that we hold dear. Claude, for instance, has its constitution—a sort of moral code.
The trouble is, these techniques don’t seem to work particularly well: Models have been shown to deliberately underperform on tests, hide their intentions, and mislead their evaluators.
Now some alignment researchers believe that reverse game theory, also known as mechanism design, might get better results. Where game theory tries to predict how rational actors will behave when given a particular set of rules, reverse game theory attempts to design rules that will elicit the kinds of behavior we want to encourage.

articles.title: Google Dismantles XCPE Botnet of 1.3 Million Android Devices
articles.summary:
Google on Monday announced the dismantling of XCPE (aka X.CPE), a backdoor and botnet of more than 1.3 million Android set-top boxes.
The malware was developed and deployed by Videostrong Technology, a China-based original equipment manufacturer and original design manufacturer (OEM/ODM) of Android devices that also operated the botnet.
Videostrong, Google says, sold access to affiliates and loaded malicious modules on the backdoored devices, which were then abused for ad fraud and data exfiltration, as residential proxies, and for loading additional malware.
“We found this malicious software built directly into many different device models and brands over multiple years, supported by dedicated infrastructure and constantly evolving configurations to evade detection and manage their affiliates,” the internet giant says.
As part of the takedown, Google took legal action to take down the botnet’s domains and servers, as well as the command-and-control (C&C) domains behind the additional modules loaded on the XCPE bots.
This likely resulted in severed access to at least 10 million other devices, as the module’s operators had diversified the distribution of their malware beyond XCPE.
Google believes the XCPE botnet was a deliberate operation by Videostrong, not the work of a rogue insider or the result of a development oversight. As such, it banned the company from making devices with preloaded Google apps.

articles.title: Valve is making changes to deal with a ‘significant increase’ in Steam game submissions
articles.summary:
In a new post today, Valve acknowledged that it’s seen “a significant increase in submissions for store and page review in recent months” and says it’s “running a little behind” by taking “up to 12 business days” for reviews instead of the typical 3-5 days.
Valve is making changes to deal with a ‘significant increase’ in Steam game submissions
Valve admits that it’s now taking ‘up to 12 business days’ to review games.
Indie developers have recently expressed frustrations over lengthy approval times for Steam games, even causing some games to miss planned launch dates. Valve says that “much” of the delay is having to re-review games, so it’s making some changes to the release checklist for developers to hopefully “cut down on re-reviews for basic functional issues.”
The changes include requiring developers to run games through Steam for at least five minutes. “Believe it or not, sometimes we review builds that have not ever been played through Steam,” Valve says. “This means that even if a game runs smoothly when a dev launches their executable directly, they might have missed basic steps that would impact a user installing and playing via Steam.”
Other requirements include making sure that achievements are ready and confirming any required common redistributables, like DirectX or Visual C++, that Steam may need to install.
Valve also says more improvements are in the works for the build review process.

Windows met aussi en pause des tâches de fond, comme l’indexation de la recherche, pendant qu’on utilise le PC.
Les applications de Microsoft ont aussi été retouchées. Sur les PC à 8 gigaoctets ou moins, les Widgets ne se chargent plus qu’à l’ouverture, ce qui libère environ 200 mégaoctets quand le panneau est fermé. Edge met en veille les onglets inactifs au bout de 15 minutes par défaut, contre deux heures jusqu’ici. Teams passe dans un mode qui consomme moins de ressources et se lance jusqu’à 20 % plus vite.
Au total, Microsoft annonce jusqu’à 900 mégaoctets de mémoire réservée en moins pendant une séance de multitâche, dont 360 mégaoctets grâce à Word, PowerPoint, Excel et Outlook.

En noviembre de 1956 la revista LIFE publicó un reportaje sobre la costumbre del hospital de la Universidad de Michigan, en Ann Arbor, de llevar animales a las plantas en las que estaban ingresados niños pequeños. El fotógrafo Francis Miller retrató a dos niñas bañando a un cerdito, a un coatí que hacía equilibrios en un cable por encima de las cabezas de los pacientes y a Peggy Kennedy, de tres años, tumbada en una cama con un respirador de plástico en el pecho mientras a su lado, en un barreño, nadaban unos patitos.
Qué le pasaba a Peggy. La culpable era la poliomielitis, una enfermedad causada por un virus diminuto que entra por la boca, casi siempre con agua o comida contaminadas con heces, y que acaba instalándose en el intestino. Allí se multiplica y, en la mayoría de los casos, la cosa no pasa de ahí. De hecho, alrededor del 70 % de los niños infectados ni siquiera llega a tener síntomas, y casi una cuarta parte pasa algo parecido a una gripe leve que se cura sola en una semana.
El problema aparece cuando el virus consigue llegar a la sangre y, a través de ella, a la médula espinal, donde ataca a un tipo de célula muy concreto, las neuronas motoras, que son las encargadas de dar a los músculos la orden de contraerse. articles.title: Synology : des pirates prennent vos fichiers en otage en exploitant des failles déjà corrigées
articles.summary:
Des NAS Synology sont la cible d'une vague d'attaques par ransomware, qui chiffre les fichiers de leurs propriétaires et réclame plusieurs milliers de dollars pour leur restitution.
Depuis la mi-octobre, les témoignages d'internautes désemparés affluent sur les Reddit et autre forums d'entraide. Photos, documents personnels, sauvegardes professionnelles… Les fichiers qu'ils avaient confiés à leur NAS sont désormais illisibles, flanqués d’une note de rançon. Dans un communiqué publié le 29 octobre, Synology a confirmé les attaques et exhorté ses clients à mettre à jour leur système d'exploitation sans attendre.
C3RB3R, un ransomware qui n'en est pas à son coup d'essai
Sur les appareils compromis, les fichiers portent désormais l'extension .L0CK3D et s'accompagnent d'un document intitulé read-me3.txt. Les pirates y expliquent avoir chiffré les données et exigent l'achat de C3rb3r Decryptor, un logiciel de déchiffrement proposé sur un portail du dark web contre plusieurs milliers de dollars. Pour convaincre leurs victimes de payer, ils offrent même de restaurer gratuitement un fichier de leur choix.
Cet outil emprunte son nom à C3RB3R, également appelé CerberImposter. Déjà repéré sur des serveurs Atlassian Confluence et GitLab, il a été déployé par le passé dans des opérations exploitant des vulnérabilités connues. Cette fois, les cybercriminels ciblent des NAS Synology exécutant d'anciennes versions de DiskStation Manager (DSM), le système qui assure leur fonctionnement.

Sa propre estimation, mise à jour ce lundi, place la chute le mercredi 4 novembre vers 10h11 heure de Paris, à 12 heures près, soit moins d’une heure d’écart avec la Space Force.
Swift n’était pas prévu pour rester aussi longtemps en orbite. Lancé en novembre 2004 pour étudier les sursauts gamma, les explosions les plus puissantes connues dans l’univers, il était prévu pour une mission de 2 ans. Son orbite …

articles.title: En 2009, unos científicos encontraron pulpos caminando con cocos por el fondo del mar. Cuando descubrieron para qué eran, quedaron atónitos
articles.summary:
En 2009, unos científicos descubrieron algo extraordinario en las aguas de Indonesia: pequeños pulpos que recogían restos y cáscaras de coco y caminaban con ellas por el fondo marino, a veces durante hasta 20 metros. Aquella forma de desplazarse era tan incómoda que los animales quedaban expuestos a sus depredadores. Hasta que los investigadores descubrieron para qué transportaban los cocos. El hallazgo terminó convirtiéndose en una de las observaciones más sorprendentes sobre la inteligencia de los invertebrados.
Una escena difícil de creer. Durante cerca de una década, los biólogos Julian Finn, Tom Tregenza y Mark Norman acumularon aproximadamente 500 horas de inmersiones en aguas de Indonesia, desde el estrecho de Lembeh hasta Bali. Estudiaban al pulpo veteado (Amphioctopus marginatus), una pequeña especie que vive sobre fondos arenosos y fangosos, cuando comenzaron a observar un comportamiento desconcertante.
Algunos ejemplares desenterraban mitades de cocos, las limpiaban con chorros de agua y las colocaban cuidadosamente bajo sus cuerpos. Después levantaban las cáscaras y comenzaban a caminar con ellas. Norman confesó que aquella escena le había resultado tan cómica que le costó contener la risa bajo el agua sin inundar su máscara de buceo.
Veinte pulpos y una conducta inexplicable. Los investigadores estudiaron a 20 ejemplares y documentaron cuatro ocasiones en las que transportaron cáscaras durante distancias de hasta 20 metros. Algunos llevaban una sola mitad, mientr…

articles.title: Nigeria’s LemFi expands beyond remittances with app rebuild, new products - Disrupt Africa

Nigerian cross-border fintech LemFi has rebuilt its app and launched a new global brand as it expands beyond remittances into savings, credit and eSIM services.
Founded in 2021 by Ridwan Olalere and Rian Cochran, LemFi lets more than two million customers send money to more than 30 countries across Africa, Asia, Europe and beyond. It processes around US$2 billion in transactions every month.
The company has now introduced savings and credit services in the UK, with other markets to follow, as well as eSIM connectivity that allows customers to buy mobile data in more than 100 destinations without changing SIM cards or paying roaming charges.
To support the expansion, LemFi has re-architected its app from the ground up so that multiple products across different countries sit within a single account. It has also launched a new brand platform, “Ambition has no passport”, which will roll out across its global markets.
“We started LemFi because sending money home was broken. What we learned is that the harder problem starts after the transfer,” said Olalere. “Our customers are building careers and businesses in one country while supporting people in another, and the financial system treats them as if they can only exist in one place at a time. We have rebuilt LemFi to work the way their lives do.”
LemFi has raised more than US$85 million to date from investors including Highland Europe, Left Lane Capital, Palm Drive Capital, Endeavor Catalyst and Y Combinator.

articles.title: Anthropic is still grappling with the economics of compute | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
There’s a lot of mystery around the finances of major AI labs, and as Anthropic inches towards it IPO, we’re starting to get some answers. In particular, the company is finally disclosing more about the economics of compute, and how much of Anthropic’s skyrocketing revenue is being lost to compute costs.
In a new filing on Monday, Anthropic released data that showed those margins on compute actually getting worse. The filing was an update to the S-1 released last week — but where that filing’s financial disclosures only covered through June 30 of this year, the new data extended to disclose results through an extra quarter, to September 30. Broadly, Anthropic had a good quarter: revenue reached $17 billion, up from $11.5 billion in the previous quarter, suggesting durable growth. But the operating loss grew at the same time, thanks in large part to growing compute costs.
Looking at the compute margins makes the picture even worse. In the new quarter, compute took up 58% of the company’s revenue, up from 48% the quarter before. At a moment when the company could win over IPO investors by showing margins improving, they’re getting worse.
A chart in the filing shows this even more clearly, tracking the company’s revenue for every dollar spent on compute. Since the start of 2025, it’s been steadily growing, peaking at just over 2x this past quarter, then falling back down to 1.72x.

articles.title: UEFI bootkit infected fully patched Windows machines. Is Microsoft to blame?
articles.summary:
In 2023, malware tracked as BlackLotus became the first publicly documented in-the-wild UEFI bootkit capable of bypassing Secure Boot on fully updated Windows 11 systems. With the industry-wide chain-of-trust mechanism subverted, the malware was able to run malicious code before Windows was fully loaded and many security defenses were operational.
Microsoft had already patched the vulnerability that BlackLotus exploited in 2022. In 2023 and 2024, Microsoft issued additional updates. The first added a new certificate that no longer trusted the vulnerable boot managers. The second provided the means to revoke trust in the digital certificate used to sign older vulnerable Windows boot managers. The organizations infected by the new bootkit, which is tracked under the name BlackX, had installed all of these patches. So how did they fall victim?
UEFI bootkit refresher
Before discussing the incident further, a brief review of BlackLotus and UEFI malware is in order. Short for Unified Extensible Firmware Interface, UEFI is firmware that runs immediately after a computer is turned on. One of its main jobs is to load system configuration settings, identify and initialize hardware components, and prepare the computer to start its OS.
Another important UEFI function is Secure Boot, a security feature that establishes a chain of trust by verifying the digital signatures of each piece of boot software before allowing it to execute. Its purpose is to prevent attackers who gain control of a…

articles.title: "Es una cuestión de salud mental": cada vez más padres están pagando hasta 260 euros la noche a niñeras nocturnas
articles.summary:
Blanca Yamira Ortiz García tiene 56 años, es puericultora y por cada noche que pasa en casa de una familia con un recién nacido cobra 260 euros, una tarifa que en un buen mes le permite ganar entre 4.000 y 5.000 euros. Su trabajo consiste en que los padres duerman mientras ella se ocupa del bebé, y hay clientas que lo tienen claro: “Para mí es una cuestión de salud mental”. Así lo cuenta un reportaje de Corriere della Sera sobre las llamadas night nannies, o niñeras nocturnas.

Entra en la casa, se quita los zapatos, se lava las manos, cambia el pañal al bebé, a menudo lo baña y después se queda despierta a oscuras mientras el resto de la familia duerme. Earlier posts in this series built the same C360 pattern with Stardog’s knowledge graph, Denodo’s data virtualization platform, AtScale’s dimensional model, and Strategy Mosaic’s linked models.
EDB Postgres AI puts the semantic layer inside the operational Postgres database as an AIDB extension. Business meaning lives next to the data in standard Postgres COMMENT statements, the join graph comes from Postgres foreign keys, and governance uses Postgres GRANT and row-level security through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint that ships with AIDB.

Tracked as CVE-2026-58115 (CVSS score of 10/10), the bug is described as a missing authentication issue on the Node-RED HTTP interface that could enable attackers to access programming nodes that can execute system commands.
Siemens disclosed it on August 11, after finding it in its SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed. SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced version 4.3.4.1 and later contain patches for the security hole.
According to Siemens, CVE-2026-58115 “could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to create malicious flows and execute arbitrary code on the underlying server with maximum privileges.”
On Sunday, VulnCheck warned that it had observed successful in-the-wild exploitation of the vulnerability on October 30. The attack came from an IP in AS8075, Microsoft’s network, and delivered a complete exploit.

At its height, x.cpe ran on more than 1.3 million Android TV devices, and unusually, these were Google-certified boxes. Google says its screening process missed the malware due to “obfuscation techniques” employed by Shenzhen-based Videostrong Technology.
In a detailed blog post, the Threat Intelligence Group explains how the x.cpe botnet evolved quickly from a single-stage dropper into a modular three-stage malware platform that sold access to third parties. Manufacturers must have their devices certified if they want access to Google apps and branding, a process that is supposed to catch threats like this. However, Videostrong’s compromised boxes, mostly sold under the MECOOL brand, evaded detection by using a backdoor to remotely install the malware after the devices were set up and online.
After devices appeared online, a stub application called x.cpe or com.oemservice would phone home. This package did not have any malicious capabilities of its own, but it had the system-level permissions necessary to install malware modules at the operator’s behest. It also disabled Play Protect, which would have otherwise flagged the silently installed packages as malicious.

Large language model hijacking attacks, also known as LLMjacking, are generating large fraudulent cloud charges, with some organizations losing more than $100,000 per day.
Companies can record costs as high as $1 million due to fraudulent calls using stolen API keys, researchers at Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant in analyzed incidents.
Based on their observations, there are "two distinct operational clusters coordinating to compromise and monetize enterprise LLM infrastructure."
The researchers identified two categories of threat actors: those who scan for publicly exposed LLM endpoints and those who steal valid API keys from unprotected machines.
After gaining initial access, the attackers sell it to services known as LLM mixers, which provide their subscribers with unauthorized access to LLMs.
Once access is resold, request volumes can spike suddenly, sometimes exceeding 1,000 requests per second. The service provider records the requests as legitimate consumption and charges the victim organization for the tokens.
GTIG and Mandiant observed an increase in this type of activity this year, with fraudulent charges exceeding $100,000 in a single day, and cumulative charges at some organizations reaching $1,000,000.
LLM mixers offer access to AI resources at very low prices, using their proxy infrastructure to relay customers' prompts to hijacked services through stolen API keys.

The filing, spotted by Business Insider, shows that Anthropic recorded more than $1.7 billion in personnel expenses from July through to September. With 5,300 people working at the company, that works out at over $322,000 per person over the three-month span, or about $107,300 per employee per month.
Those costs include standard cash salaries along with bonuses, benefits, and employer payroll taxes. The largest share, $1.1 billion, came from Anthropic's stock-based compensation expenses, which reflect the value of company shares employees earn as part of their pay. articles.title: LinkedIn Uses OpenTelemetry to Trace the Member Journey from Tap to Backend
articles.summary:
LinkedIn has built an OpenTelemetry-based telemetry platform that connects what members do in its iOS, Android, and web applications with the backend services processing those interactions.
The goal is to close a common observability gap. Client analytics can show that a member tapped a button or encountered an error, while backend tracing explains what happened inside the services handling the request. Historically, connecting these views required engineers to correlate separate systems. LinkedIn's approach allows a member interaction to be followed from the client through frontend and backend services to the underlying data stores.
A single page can generate numerous requests, each potentially passing through multiple services. LinkedIn introduced a pageForestId to provide context above individual distributed traces.
Each request retains its OpenTelemetry traceId, while related requests from the same page context can be associated through the pageForestId. Engineers can therefore investigate both an individual request and the wider activity that contributed to a member's experience.
This is important because conventional distributed tracing generally follows one request, whereas a member journey can involve many related requests.

AI agents that interact with enterprise APIs on behalf of users need to maintain user identity throughout the request chain. This breaks audit trails, bypasses user-level access controls, and violates the principle of least privilege.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. An AI agent can then call the ServiceNow REST API while preserving the calling user’s identity. You configure the token exchange on the gateway target, and AgentCore Gateway performs the exchange on each request. The pattern can be applied to other REST APIs protected by OAuth.

Mazin Gilbert, executive director of the Linux Foundation’s Agentic AI Foundation, left Google earlier this year to lead the new AAIF, and he recently shared with The New Stack a truth central to its mission: The AAIF has to move faster than its members.

All of this is happening while the foundation’s own members are often still figuring out how to build and use agents themselves. Some contribute to protocols and ship products, but others are still trying to get their agents out of the lab and into production. articles.title: Google will let schools skip AI tools, but they have to give up search, too
articles.summary:
While Google is trying to move beyond Chromebooks, the ubiquity of these devices has made the company’s education products huge in schools. Now, Google says it will let educators choose whether to allow its AI tools in the classroom. However, blocking AI tools also means giving up search, leaving schools with a difficult decision.
Google’s new overarching approach to AI in K-12 classrooms sounds good on the surface. After consulting educators, researchers, and lawmakers, Google has decided that schools using its education products will be opted out of AI tools by default. It will be up to administrators to manually enable them when these changes roll out in the coming months.
When you look at what Google considers to be an AI tool, the nature of the Faustian bargain becomes clear. The affected products are Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search. There’s no picking and choosing—you either allow all the AI or none of it.
This is actually consistent with Google’s approach in the consumer space. Google executives have said in no uncertain terms that Google Search is AI search. Most searches now provide an AI Overview at the top, and the company is constantly coming up with new ways to nudge people toward the conversational AI Mode chatbot function. Google sees this as the future.

The federal government’s AI-powered translation tool, GCtranslate, has only been around for about six months, but in that time, it’s racked up a concerning number of errors, including some really unfortunate translations.
According to documents CBC/Radio-Canada obtained through a Freedom of Information Act request, GCTranslate introduced several mistranslations and hallucinations in government documents, particularly when used for translations from English to French.
Errors range from simpler mistakes, like translating a common abbreviation for the transportation bureau, TB, to Tuberculosis, to more severe errors, like changing someone’s name from “Mike” to “Stephanie.” There were also some other funny translation errors, such as the tool translating “Buy Canadian Policy” into “Achetez une politique canadienne,” which means “Buy a Canadian policy.”
One of the more… unfortunate changes spotted by Radio-Canada was translating a shorthand for “cumulative growth” to “sperme croissance,” which certainly does not mean cumulative growth.
Bad (and funny) translation mistakes might seem innocuous, but they can have an outsized impact on Canadians. Some ideas weren’t the best, either, like demonstrably worse human-machine interfaces that add to driver distraction; yet, they still proliferated throughout the industry and across the cars offered for sale. But the good news is that the pushback seems to be working.
“When the trend of the Piano Black and the switchless interior was happening, it was during a time when designers and companies and engineers and everybody were thinking that, ‘Hey, we can just get rid of all these switches on the interior. We can put it all in the software. It’ll save money. It’ll save us tooling up all these extra parts for unique cars and all this stuff and make the interior more like a software experience.’ And it was done with those intentions,” said Hiren Patel, senior design manager at Nissan.
That resulted in cars with minimalist interiors that looked good in the dealership. But people drive their cars on roads; they don’t just sit inside them, parked inside a dealership. “So lots of people were complaining about it and saying, ‘Hey, it takes my eyes off the road to change the temperature or to adjust my seat or do whatever.’ It’s not as easy as doing something on your phone where it’s just right at your fingertips and intuitive,” Patel said.

articles.title: Vitest 5: Prioritises Performance with a Shared Vite Server, Trace View, and Stricter Test Defaults

Vitest, the Vite-native testing framework maintained by VoidZero, has released Vitest 5.0, a major version that puts raw speed ahead of new surface area while quietly tightening several long-standing defaults.
Using a purpose-built benchmark suite that spans everything from a five-file utility package to a 1,280-module monolith, the team reports gains of roughly 8 to 25 percent across most setups, rising to 53 percent in VM pool scenarios. VoidZero summarised the release on X as "vm pools up to 53% faster, ~18% boost across the board including Browser Mode". The wins come from inline projects sharing a single Vite server, a stabilised on-disk fsModuleCache, fewer round trips between the main process and workers, and VM pools that reuse compiled code. A new vitest doctor command reruns a suite under alternative configurations and recommends faster options.

articles.title: CentOS co-founder creates a Linux-compatible kernel in just 11 days, with AI doing almost all the coding
articles.summary:
The big picture: Writing an operating system kernel from scratch usually takes a team of seasoned engineers years of work. Gregory Kurtzer, who co-founded CentOS and later launched Rocky Linux, says he just built one in 11 days – mostly by having an AI agent write the code. Even without any Linux code underneath, his new kernel can already boot Rocky Linux 10. That said, it's still very much a research prototype.
Kurtzer unveiled the kernel, Ginux, on X last week. The code is on GitHub, too, under the Apache 2.0 license. As for the name, it blends Linux, GPT, and Greg. The README jokes that to keep its author's ego in check, the G officially stands for GPT.
Despite the name, Ginux isn't a fork of Linux. Everything from memory management and scheduling to filesystems and networking was written from scratch, mostly in Rust. What it does share with Linux is the ABI, so unmodified Linux programs can run on it as-is.
Its README describes Linux as a "personality" the kernel presents to software. That's the only one built so far, though BSD is floated as a possibility down the line.
Even that one personality still has plenty of gaps, though. Of the 375 system calls in Linux 6.12's x86-64 interface, Ginux fully implements just 82. Another 245 only partly work. The remaining 48 are blocked on purpose.
Software on Ginux runs inside isolated "domains," each with its own processes, memory, and filesystem. The project pitches these as a stronger boundary than containers, though Ginux stil…

articles.title: Hackers hijack cPGuard autoupdate to deploy backdoor, steal data
articles.summary:
Attackers have compromised the update infrastructure for the cPGuard web security suite to distribute a backdoor and a data-stealing script.
OpsShield, the cPGuard developer, published an alert earlier today saying the attack began on November 2 at 02:06 UTC and affected versions 5.88.12 through 5.88.19.
The vendor says that it detected the compromise and stopped the malicious distribution within 12 hours after the attacker pushed the compromised cPGuard versions.
Although the company could not confirm, it said that some servers may have not received and run the malicious script due to update checks occurring at specific intervals.
The attacker leveraged legitimate credentials to gain initial access, although it remains unclear how they were obtained.
“On 2 November 2026 at 02:06 UTC, an unidentified attacker used compromised credentials to gain unauthorized access to OpsShield’s update distribution infrastructure (CDN),” OpsShield said.
“The attacker used this access to distribute a malicious script through the cPGuard update channel.”
cPGuard is a Linux web-server security suite offering malware scanning, firewalls, and attack protection.
It is commonly used by hosting firms and server administrators alongside panels such as cPanel, DirectAdmin, and Plesk. Namecheap offers it on VPS and dedicated servers.

articles.title: Google Launches LiteRT Tensor API for Building, Customizing, and Optimizing ML Models for On-Device
articles.summary:
Google has introduced the LiteRT Tensor API, a lightweight C++ API that allows developers to build, customize, and optimize machine learning models directly for on-device execution. According to Google, it combines the flexibility of native model authoring with cross-platform portability.
The traditional approach, Google says, is for developers to write computations manually in C++ for maximum control, which comes with a significant drawback:
Implementations are tightly coupled to specific backends (such as Metal, OpenCL, or Vulkan) and must be rewritten for each new hardware target. Furthermore, managing zero-copy buffer interoperability and synchronization across CPU, GPU, and NPU, while gluing together pre-processing, inference, and post-processing, demands substantial manual engineering effort.
The LiteRT Tensor API aims to address these challenges by allowing developers to build computation graphs operation by operation in C++. This provided greater control over model architecture, optimization, and accelerator execution, while enabling the same graphs to run through LiteRT on CPU, GPU, and NPU hardware without requiring a rewrite for each new target.

Australia passed its under-16 social media law in 2024, and the restrictions took effect on December 10, 2025, making it the first country to introduce a ban that has since spread around the world.
The law requires platforms including Facebook, Instagram, Kick, Reddit, Snapchat, Threads, TikTok, Twitch, X (formerly Twitter), and YouTube to take reasonable steps to prevent Australians under 16 from creating or keeping accounts. Companies that fail to do so face court-imposed civil penalties of up to AU$109.2 million (about $76 million).
Unsurprisingly, these companies weren't happy about the change, especially Reddit. Soon after the law was introduced, Steve Huffman's firm challenged the law, emphasized that the platform is a "collection of public fora," rather than a social media site. It also filed a lawsuit in Australia's High Court to overturn the ban or, failing that, make itself exempt.
Reddit and a libertarian advocacy group say the law should be declared invalid because it violates an implied freedom of political expression in the country's constitution.

articles.title: Fibre cuts threaten Nigeria's digital economy, who pays?

When Nigeria’s president, Bola Tinubu, signed the Designation and Protection of Critical National Information Infrastructure (CNII) Order in June 2024, the Federal Government aimed to shield telecommunications assets from relentless vandalism and physical damage. By classifying fibre lines, base stations, and data centres as vital national security installations, the order sought to impose deterrent penalties and curb unauthorised tampering.
Yet two years on, chronic breaches continue to impose steep financial penalties on operators, diverting capital from network expansion to nonstop emergency repairs and destabilising internet reliability across the country.
In 2023, before the order, MTN Nigeria suffered more than 6,000 fibre cuts in a single year—averaging roughly 16-17 severed lines per day.
Fast-forward to 2025, past the presidential order: the numbers increased; between January and July, the telco recorded 5,478 fibre cuts. That pushed its daily average to over 26 snapped cables.
In plain terms, instead of scaring reckless diggers and vandals away and improving coordination between construction firms and other key stakeholders, the new rules led MTN Nigeria to fix about eight more broken cables per day than before the order was introduced.

Dicho a muy grosso modo, creará pequeños eclipses artificiales para centrar toda la atención en los exoplanetas que se quieran analizar.

articles.title: Hacienda obliga a tributar por las propinas que reciben los trabajadores, pero cotizarán si lo recoge el convenio o las gestiona la empresa
articles.summary:
Cualquier tipo de propina que reciban los trabajadores de bares y restaurantes tiene repercusiones fiscales. Es decir, que aunque los clientes den la propina de manera voluntaria, esto va a suponer que los trabajadores deben tenerlo en cuenta a la hora de calcular los rendimientos del trabajo (impuesto sobre la renta de las personas físicas). Además de ello, debe analizarse si deben cotizar a la Seguridad Social.
El IRPF alcanza a las propinas
En primer lugar, en el artículo 17.1 de la Ley del IRPF están incluidas las cantidades que provienen directa o indirectamente de la relación de trabajo o del propio trabajo personal. Es decir, que además de los salarios se incluyen otros rendimientos relacionados con el trabajo (utilidades). En este sentido, las propinas que reciben de los clientes van a estar sujetas al IRPF.
Además, están previstas las retenciones. En efecto, en el artículo 76 del Reglamento del IRPF se habla de los casos en que el que realiza la actividad económica tiene que abonar a sus trabajadores las cantidades que los terceros le entreguen en concepto de propinas. En el caso de que sean repartidas por la empresa, deberá realizar en su caso la correspondiente retención (que se ingresará en Hacienda).
Es importante destacar que estar sometido a IRPF quiere decir que están en la base de dicho impuesto. Sin embargo, no es necesario que haya obligación de presentar la declaración (ver artículo 96 de la ley).

Sous ses airs de divertissement entre joueurs, la pratique sert aussi à diffuser de la propagande et à recruter, jusque chez les mineurs. "The CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin from 1.2.1 to 1.2.2 does not apply an authorization check on one of its AJAX endpoints, allowing unauthenticated users to invoke administrative operations, including deleting arbitrary files on the server, overwriting the payment gateway configuration and recovering stored wallet credentials in cleartext," according to a description of the flaw on the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD).
The vulnerability affects versions 1.2.1 through 1.2.2, which is the latest version. There are no known fixes for the flaw, according to WP Scan. As of August 28, 2026, the plugin has been closed on the WordPress Plugin Directory and is no longer available for download due to an unspecified "security issue."
Statistics show that the plugin has been collectively downloaded 1,845 times, including 20 downloads over the last seven days. It's unclear if it's actively installed on any WordPress sites.

articles.title: Attackers Exploit Critical Siemens IoT2050 Flaw to Plant Remote Command Backdoors
articles.summary:
A maximum-severity security flaw impacting Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices has come under active exploitation, VulnCheck has revealed.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-58115 (CVSS score: 10.0), is a case of missing authentication for a critical function that could be exploited by an unauthenticated remote attacker to run arbitrary code.
"SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed contain a missing authentication vulnerability in the Node-RED HTTP interface that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to create malicious flows and execute arbitrary code on the underlying server with maximum privileges," Siemens said in an advisory released back in August 2026.
The issue has been remediated in versions 4.3.4.1 or later. As mitigations, Siemens recommends that users uninstall Node-RED or harden the installation by following the steps below -
- Enabling HTTPS access

Lancé en novembre 2004, Swift est un observatoire spatial qui embarquait trois télescopes pour observer les sursauts gamma, ces explosions parmi les plus violentes et lumineuses de l’univers. Conçu initialement pour durer quelques années en orbite terrestre basse, l’appareil a largement dépassé ses objectifs en cartographiant plus de 2 000 sursauts gamma et autant de supernovas. Mais la hausse de l’activité solaire en 2024 a accéléré sa descente, scellant le sort de ce satellite qui n’a pas de système de propulsion pour rectifier sa trajectoire.
La fin d’une mission historique
L’échec de la mission de sauvetage LINK, lancée en juillet 2026 pour 30 millions de dollars, a sonné le glas du télescope. Des soucis de système de contrôle ont empêché ce vaisseau robotique de stabiliser Swift pour le remonter sur une orbite plus sûre. Descendu à moins de 270 kilomètres d’altitude, le satellite a réalisé sa toute dernière observation le 20 octobre dernier avant que l’équipe de l’université d’État de Pennsylvanie ne coupe définitivement ses systèmes.
Pendant plus de deux décennies, les données récoltées par Swift ont nourri plus de 7 000 articles de recherche. Shawn Domagal-Goldman, directeur de la division astrophysique au siège de la NASA, salue un investissement extrêmement rentable qui aura profondément transformé notre compréhension de l’univers. Même hors service, les archives laissées par l’appareil continueront d’alimenter les découvertes scientifiques pendant des décennies.

C'est un clap de fin pour deux casques Meta Quest, début 2027, ces deux anciennes versions verront leur suivi logiciel se terminer et ne seront plus mis à jour.
Meta prépare l'arrêt du support logiciel de ses casques Quest 2 et Quest Pro. Selon une annonce publiée sur le blog de la société destiné aux développeurs, les dernières mises à jour du système d'exploitation sont prévues pour mars 2027. Les deux appareils ne deviendront pas inutilisables pour autant. Les casques continueront de fonctionner, avec des correctifs de sécurité jusqu'à la fin de l'année 2027.
Un calendrier en deux temps
Après mars 2027, les casques ne recevront plus de mises à jour du système. Les mises à jour de sécurité, elles, se poursuivront jusqu'à la fin de 2027.
Le Quest 2, lancé en 2020, aura ainsi bénéficié d'un peu plus de sept ans de support de sécurité. Le Quest Pro, arrivé en octobre 2022, aura quant à lui eu droit à seulement cinq ans. Quel dommage d'acheter une version plus onéreuse pour avoir un support moins durable.

Un seul SMS piégé suffit à couper la ligne d’un téléphone non mis à jour, appels d’urgence compris. Et la victime ne voit rien, puisque le message n’arrive jamais dans sa messagerie.
Huit octets pour faire tomber la partie téléphone
L’attaque passe par les SMS WAP Push, des messages techniques que les opérateurs utilisent pour envoyer des réglages, et qu’Android traite tout seul en arrière-plan. Le message piégé ne pèse que huit octets. Son en-tête annonce une longueur négative, et Android plante en essayant de réserver la mémoire correspondante. Le processus com.android.phone, qui gère les appels et le réseau mobile, s’arrête alors une à deux secondes. Avec une vingtaine de messages, le téléphone peut rester coincé dans une boucle de redémarrages.
Sur un appareil sous Android 12, le chercheur a vu le téléphone repartir toutes les 90 secondes environ sur son menu de secours. Seule une réinitialisation d’usine, qui efface tout le contenu, l’a débloqué.
